name: ICO
quick_answer: ICO — Icon file format used for application icons, favicons, and desktop shortcut images, storing multiple resolutions in a single container.
definition: ICO is an image file format. Icon file format used for application icons, favicons, and desktop shortcut images, storing multiple resolutions in a single container. It is commonly used in workflows that require reliable image handling and is supported by a wide range of applications and online tools.

use_cases.title: Website favicons
use_cases.text: ICO is the standard format for the favicon displayed in browser tabs, bookmarks, and address bars for websites.

use_cases.title: Windows application icons
use_cases.text: ICO is the native icon format on Windows, used for executable files, desktop shortcuts, folders, and taskbar icons.

use_cases.title: Multi-resolution icon containers
use_cases.text: ICO files store multiple icon sizes (16x16 to 256x256) in a single file so the OS automatically uses the most appropriate resolution.

use_cases.title: Browser tab and bookmark icons
use_cases.text: Browsers request favicon.ico automatically from the website root and display it in tabs, bookmarks, and history entries.

use_cases.title: Desktop shortcut and system graphics
use_cases.text: ICO is used for custom desktop shortcut icons on Windows, giving applications and files a recognizable visual identity on the desktop.

advantages.title: Multi-resolution container
advantages.text: ICO stores multiple icon sizes (typically 16x16 up to 256x256) in one file so the OS and browser always use the most appropriate size.

advantages.title: Native OS integration on Windows
advantages.text: ICO is recognized natively by Windows Explorer, the taskbar, and the Start menu without any additional software.

advantages.title: Transparency support
advantages.text: ICO supports full alpha transparency in 32-bit variants, allowing icons to appear cleanly over any background color or wallpaper.

advantages.title: Universal browser favicon support
advantages.text: Every browser automatically requests favicon.ico from the website root, making ICO the most broadly compatible favicon format.

limitations.title: Not suitable for general images
limitations.text: ICO is designed exclusively for icons and favicons and is not appropriate for photographs, illustrations, or everyday image sharing.

limitations.title: Complex to create without dedicated tools
limitations.text: Generating a valid multi-resolution ICO file manually is non-trivial; dedicated tools or converters are typically required.

limitations.title: Limited color depth in small sizes
limitations.text: Older ICO sizes (16x16, 32x32) have historically supported limited color depths, which can reduce visual quality for complex icons.

limitations.title: Primarily a Windows-centric format
limitations.text: Outside of favicons and Windows applications, ICO has limited use on macOS, Linux, or cross-platform systems.

comparisons.title: ICO vs PNG
comparisons.text: ICO stores multiple icon resolutions in a single container optimized for Windows and browser favicons, while PNG is simpler and preferred for single-size modern web favicons.

comparisons.title: ICO vs SVG
comparisons.text: ICO is a raster container optimized for Windows and multi-resolution browser favicons, while SVG is a resolution-independent vector format preferred for scalable icons on modern devices.

comparisons.title: ICO vs BMP
comparisons.text: ICO is a specialized icon container with multi-resolution support and transparency, while BMP is a simple uncompressed raster format without icon-specific features.

faq.question: What is an ICO file?
faq.answer: An ICO file is an icon container format used for website favicons, Windows application icons, and desktop shortcuts, storing multiple resolutions in one file.

faq.question: What size should a favicon ICO be?
faq.answer: A favicon.ico typically contains 16x16 and 32x32 pixel images at minimum. Including 48x48 and 256x256 improves appearance on high-DPI displays and taskbars.

faq.question: Can ICO files contain multiple sizes?
faq.answer: Yes, ICO is specifically designed to bundle multiple resolutions in a single file so the operating system or browser picks the most suitable size automatically.

faq.question: Should I use ICO or PNG for my favicon?
faq.answer: ICO provides the best compatibility across all browsers including older IE versions. PNG favicons are supported by modern browsers and are simpler to produce.

faq.question: How do I create an ICO file from PNG?
faq.answer: You can convert a PNG to ICO using online converters or image editors that support ICO export. Many favicon generators accept PNG input and produce multi-size ICO files.

faq.question: Is ICO supported on macOS?
faq.answer: macOS uses ICNS as its native icon format. ICO files can be opened with some tools on macOS but the format is primarily used in Windows and web contexts.
